source.title: From Real to Synthetic: Synthesizing Millions of Diversified and Complicated User Instructions with Attributed Grounding
source.authors: Chiwei Zhu; Benfeng Xu; Xiao-Rui Wang; Zhen-Dong Mao

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some referenced figures are not rendered in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Reports downstream benchmark results as instruction-tuning data scale increases, extending scale-related evaluation to supervised fine-tuning data volume. It does not test pretraining loss scaling or model-size scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper tests instruction-data scale and reports downstream benchmark performance. Results comparing datasets, ablations, and model sizes are not rows unless they report the effect of scale on the claim-relevant behavior.
record.test_reason: The scaling experiment (Section 6.2, Appendix H) varies the size of the authors' own SFT dataset. It reports Alpaca Eval 2.0 scores of their own method, not pretraining loss and not downstream performance against model or pretraining scale. No power law is fitted, and nothing is extrapolated. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as motivation for scale. This is a related but different construct (instruction-data volume vs downstream score), so it goes under fits_no_version rather than V5 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say LLaMA-3-8B Alpaca Eval performance improves consistently with SynthQuestions data scale, and that Qwen-2.5-7B shows 'similar trends' (a positive relation from 100K to 400K). They take this as showing that synthesizing more data could further improve capability. They did not test beyond 1M, and the Qwen 800K and 1M runs are deferred.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales supervised instruction-tuning data and evaluates downstream benchmarks; it does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy across parameter, token, or compute scales.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by evaluation metric: Qwen-2.5-7B Alpaca Eval LC increases from 100K to 400K, while WR dips at 200K.

fits_no_version.finding: LLaMA-3-8B Alpaca Eval 2.0 is reported to improve consistently as SynthQuestions SFT data grows over 2^i·100K subsets up to 1M (values not rendered). Qwen-2.5-7B LC rises 17.25→17.89→18.19 from 100K to 400K, while WR is flat or noisy (16.03, 14.64, 16.04).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream instruction-following benchmark scores rise monotonically with supervised fine-tuning data volume.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (venue stated in the supplied metadata); the paper text also identifies itself as a preprint/work in progress.
record.problems: The main LLaMA-3-8B scale-curve values are available only in an unrendered figure in the supplied text. The study tests instruction-data scale only up to 1M, and the Qwen scale table stops at 400K with 800K and 1M deferred. WR is not monotonic in the reported Qwen results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant scale results were stated as separate numerical outcomes beyond the Figure 7 description and Appendix H Table 14.

untested.parts: Pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute: not measured.
No shape or architecture variation at fixed parameter count.
Fine-tuning data is varied, but no loss is measured and no power-law form is fitted or tested.
No downstream performance against model scale or pretraining loss. Only SFT data volume is varied, for 8B and 7B base models.
No comparison of fits or exponents.

missing.what: Numeric Alpaca Eval 2.0 values for the LLaMA-3-8B data-scale sweep (100K to 1M)

record.verdict_notes: This is a data-synthesis paper; the scaling result concerns the authors' own dataset size during SFT. The Qwen differences are within about one SD of the benchmark, so the record's 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels for V6 are dropped.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameter count, training tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation of loss laws from small pretraining runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations as compute changes.
Effects of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss behavior in other modalities or training regimes.

The study varies instruction-tuning data volume, not model size or pretraining loss; it does not establish predictability from pretraining loss or generalize beyond its tested models, benchmarks, and data scales.
Dependence of pretraining scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices and setup.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Trained on randomly sampled subsets of SYNTHQUESTIONS at increasing data scales.

conditions.value: SYNTHQUESTIONS subsets of 2^i · 100K from a 1M dataset

rows.measure: Alpaca Eval 2.0 performance; specific metric values are not stated in the text.
rows.value: The text states that performance consistently improves as the training-set scale increases.
rows.note: Figure 7 is referenced but its plotted values and metric labels are not available in the supplied text.
rows.check: Measures downstream score against SFT data volume for the authors' own dataset, not model or pretraining scale. Figure 7 values are not in the text; only the claim that performance 'consistently improves' is stated. No functional form is reported.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5-7B
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a 100K subset of SYNTHQUESTIONS.
rows.note: The table compares this result with the 200K and 400K data-scale conditions.
rows.check: A single 100K data point with no comparison. It is the baseline for r3 and r4, not a result on its own. SFT data scale, not a claim version.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5-7B
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a 200K subset of SYNTHQUESTIONS.
rows.note: The LC score rises relative to the reported 100K result.
rows.check: The baseline should be r2 (17.25). The rise to 17.89 is within one SD (~1.1), so it is not clearly an effect. SFT data scale, not a claim version.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5-7B
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a 400K subset of SYNTHQUESTIONS.
rows.note: The LC score rises relative to the reported 100K and 200K results.
rows.check: The baseline should be r2. The rise from 17.25 to 18.19 over a 4x data increase is about one SD. SFT data scale, not a claim version.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5-7B
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a 100K subset of SYNTHQUESTIONS.
rows.note: The table reports WR alongside the data-scale conditions.
rows.check: A single 100K WR point; it is the baseline for r6 and r7. SFT data scale, not a claim version.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5-7B
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a 200K subset of SYNTHQUESTIONS.
rows.note: WR is lower than the reported 100K result despite the increase in training data.
rows.check: Labelled reversed, but the drop from 16.03 to 14.64 is about 1.3 SD, roughly within noise. SFT data scale, not a claim version.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5-7B
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a 400K subset of SYNTHQUESTIONS.
rows.note: WR at 400K is slightly above the reported 100K result and above the 200K result.
rows.check: 16.04 vs 16.03 at 100K is no change, yet the record marks it observed. SFT data scale, not a claim version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
